title: Evaluation of Physical Activity for Prevention of Atrial Fibrillation Recurrence
summary: PA-in-AF is a multicenter, randomized feasibility study for patients aged 30 to 75 who are undergoing their first catheter ablation for non-permanent atrial fibrillation. Informed consent may be obtained prior to ablation or during the early follow-up period after ablation. Following a trial period with the wearable device and the collection of baseline data 2–3 months after ablation, participants are randomized into one of two groups. One group receives exercise coaching guided by the wearable device, while the other group receives standard aftercare. Participants in both groups wear a portable device and receive technical support as needed. Only the coaching group receives structured exercise support, regular feedback, and personalized recommendations for gradually increasing activity. The activity goal is 240 heart rate zone minutes per week.

interventions.name: Arm 1 (Intervention to promote physical activity using wearables): A predominantly remote, wearable-driven, and tiered intervention to promote physical activity, featuring wearable-based monitoring, adaptive weekly data-driven feedback according to a predetermined escalation algorithm, technical sup

Arm 2 (control group): Standard care following VHF ablation and wearable-based monitoring without movement goals, exercise coaching, or feedback on physical activity. Technical support, safety instructions, and the procedure for handling VHF alerts are the same as those for the intervention group.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age 30–75 years; first catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation with pulmonary vein isolation; enrolment before the end of the blanking period (maximum 3 months after PVI); suitability and motivation to participate in physical activity; written informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
Previous catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation before the index PVI; valvular atrial fibrillation; permanent atrial fibrillation; overt heart failure with left ventricular ejection fraction <30%; pacemaker or implantable cardioverter-defibrillator if this interferes with MRI examinations; myocardial infarction or cardiac surgery within the previous 12 months or planned cardiac surgery; autoimmune disease, active malignancy or other systemic inflammatory disease; previous organ transplantation; inability to participate in a structured physical activity programme due to a musculoskeletal disorder; competitive sports or regular physical activity >10 hours/week; other reasons that, in the investigator’s judgment, make participation unsafe or impracticable, such as a relevant language barrier. Participants with AF recurrence requiring repeat PVI will not be randomized.
